name: Mirroring
definition: Repeat the last 1-3 critical words of opponent's last sentence as a question to get them to elaborate and feel understood.

name: Labeling
definition: Name the emotion opponent is feeling. Must start with 'It seems like...' / 'It looks like...' / 'It sounds like...' + emotion.

name: Accusation Audit
definition: Proactively list the worst things opponent could be thinking about you before they say it, starting with 'You probably think...'.

name: Calibrated Question
definition: Ask open-ended How or What questions that make opponent feel in control while forcing them to solve your problem.

name: No-Oriented Question
definition: Ask questions phrased so that 'No' is the safe answer, removing feelings of entrapment (e.g., 'Have you given up on...?').

name: Tactical Empathy
definition: Actively tune into the counterpart's perspective and feelings to intentionally build rapid rapport and trust.

name: The 'That's Right' Summary
definition: Combine labeling and paraphrasing to summarize their situation until they respond with 'That's right', signaling total alignment.

name: Bending Reality (Loss Aversion)
definition: Frame choices around what the counterpart stands to lose rather than gain, leveraging human loss aversion.

name: Extreme Anchoring
definition: Set an extreme initial reference point or baseline to drastically adjust expectations before making a realistic offer.

name: Ackerman Bargaining
definition: Use a structured 4-step counteroffer process (65%, 85%, 95%, 100% of target) using precise non-round numbers and a final non-monetary item.

name: The Rule of 3
definition: Get the counterpart to agree to the same commitment 3 distinct times using different techniques to confirm genuine buy-in.

name: Uncovering Black Swans
definition: Identify hidden pieces of unknown information or underlying motivations that completely alter the balance of leverage.

name: 7-38-55 Rule
definition: Evaluate emotional intent through 7% spoken words, 38% tone of voice, and 55% body language to spot insincerity.

name: Late-Night FM DJ Voice
definition: Speak with a deep, slow, downward-inflecting voice to instantly calm down tension and project absolute control.

name: Forced Problem Solving ('How am I supposed to do that?')
definition: Deliver a graceful refusal using 'How am I supposed to do that?' to make the opponent confront your limitations and solve them for you.

name: Guaranteeing Execution
definition: Ask implementation questions ('How will we know we're on track?') to ensure the deal is actually actionable behind the scenes.

name: Pronoun Discounting
definition: Track pronoun usage; heavy use of 'I/me' indicates low authority, while 'we/they' often signals the true decision-maker.

name: Pivot to Non-Monetary Terms
definition: Offer high-value, low-cost non-monetary items or terms when numeric concessions reach an impasse.

name: Odd-Specific Numbers
definition: State numbers that look precise and non-round (e.g., $37,845 instead of $38,000) so they feel unyielding and thoroughly calculated.

name: The Email Magic Question
definition: Send the one-line trigger 'Have you given up on this project?' to provoke a fast 'No' from a ghosting counterpart.
